questions.question:
Leukemia is a type of human disease which is

A. a cancer of the white blood cells

B. caused by a deficiency of vitamins

C. cancer in the brain

D. caused by an overdose of proteins
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Option 2**__ i.e **A**.

__
 
• **Leukemia** is a type of **blood cancer** caused by an increase in the number of **white blood cells (WBC)** in the body.
 
• WBCs protect our body from foreign substances.
 
• Some **Vitamin** deficiency diseases:
 
 
• **Vitamins A** deficiency causes **blindness**.
 
• **Vitamins D** deficiency causes **Rickets (Bone abnormalities)**.
 
• **Vitamin E** deficiency causes **Neurological problems.**
 
• **Vitamin K** deficiency causes **Blood clotting problems.**
 
 
 
• **Amyloidosis** is a disease that occurs due to **abnormal intake of proteins**.
 
• Fatigue and weakness, shortness of breath are common symptoms of this disease.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• White blood cells play a crucial role in the immune system. They fight infections and protect the body from disease.
 
• In leukemia, the bone marrow produces abnormal white blood cells. These cells are not functional and can crowd out healthy blood cells, leading to various health problems.
 
• Leukemia can be acute or chronic. Acute leukemia progresses rapidly, while chronic leukemia develops more slowly.
 
• There are several types of leukemia, each with different characteristics and treatments.

**Here's why the other options are incorrect:**

 
• B. caused by a deficiency of vitamins: Vitamin deficiencies can weaken the immune system and increase the risk of infection, **but they are not directly related to leukemia.**
 
• C. cancer in the brain: While some cancers can spread to the brain, including **leukemia, it is not primarily a brain cancer.**
 
• D. caused by an overdose of proteins: An overdose of proteins can have** negative health consequences, but it is not a known cause of leukemia.**

questions.question:
Two pipes, A & B can fill a tank in 12 & 16 minutes respectively. Both pipes are together, but 4 minutes before the tank is full, pipe A is closed. In how many minutes will the tank be full?

A. 9 minutes 8 seconds

B. 10 minutes 9 seconds

C. 11 minutes 19 seconds

D. 11 minutes 29 seconds
questions.solution:
Let, the tank will be full in x minutes

According to the questions,

⇒ (x – 4)/12 + x/16 = 1

⇒ [4(x – 4) + 3x]/48 = 1

⇒ 7x – 16 = 48

⇒ 7x = 64

⇒ x = 64/7

Rightarrow x = 9(1)/(7)

∴ In 9(1)/(7) mins = 9 minutes 8 seconds the tank will be full

questions.question:
Construction of the Qutub Minar, the world’s tallest brick minaret commenced in 1193, under the orders of ______ the founder of the Delhi Sultanate.

A. Firoz Shah Tughlaq.

B. Qutub-ud-din Aibak.

C. Iltutmish.

D. Quli Qutub Shah.
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Option 3**__ i.e __**B**__.

 
• **Qutab-ud-din Aibak**:

 
 
• **Qutab Minar** is a soaring, 73 m-high tower of victory, built-in 1193 by** Qutab-ud-din Aibak** immediately after the defeat of Delhi's last Hindu kingdom.
 
• The tower has five distinct storeys.
 
• The first three stories are made of red sandstone; the fourth and fifth storeys are of marble and sandstone.
 
• At the foot of the tower is the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque, the first mosque to be built in India.
 
• Qutab-ud-din Aibak was the **first Muslim ruler of Delhi,** ruled from 1206 to 1210 AD.
 
 
 
• **Firoz Shah Tughlaq**:
 
 
• He was the third ruler of the Tughlaq dynasty that ruled over Delhi from 1351 to 1388 AD.
 
• He established the **Diwan-i-Khairat** -- office for charity
 
• He established the** Diwan-i-Bundagan **-- department of slave
 
• He is known to establish four new towns, Firozabad, Fatehabad, Jaunpur and Hissar
 
 
 
• **Iltutmish**:
 
 
• He succeeded to the throne after Qutub-ud-din-Aibak.
 
• He was the third ruler of the Delhi Sultanate, belonging to the **Mamluk dynasty**.
 
• He constituted a corp of forty loyal slave Amirs known as **Turkan-i-Chihalgani** also called **Chalisa**.
 
• He completed the building of Qutab Minar.
 
 
 
• **Quli Qutub Shah (1565-1612)**:
 
 
• He was the fifth sultan of the** Qutb Shahi dynasty of Golkonda**
 
• He founded the city of **Hyderabad**, in South-central India and built its architectural centerpiece, the Charminar.
 
• Muhammed Quli Qutub Shah had the distinction of being the first Saheb-e-dewan Urdu poet.

• **Andhra Pradesh**:
 
 
• Kuchipudi is a dance-drama performance art that originated in a village of Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh, India.
 
• Kuchipudi is not only a dance but a fine amalgamation of dance, gestures, speech, and song.
 
 
 
• **Karnataka**:
 
 
• Yakshagana is an Indian traditional theatre art form that originated in Karnataka.
 
• It is a temple art form that depicts mythological stories and Puranas.
 
 
 
• **Tamil Nadu**:
 
 
• Kummi is one of the most important and ancient forms of village dances of Tamil Nadu. 
 
• It originated when there were no musical instruments, with the participants clapping their hands to keep time

questions.solution:

• He is also regarded as the "father of Qawwali".
 
 
 
• **Baiju Bawra (1542-1613)**:
 
 
• Baiju was one of the most prominent Dhrupad singers and composers in the medieval period.
 
• He was under the patronage of Raja Mansingh Tomar in Gwalior.
 
• Baiju learned Dhrupad music in Dagurvaani in Vrindavan under Swami Haridas (1512–1607).
 
• He was called Bawra (crazy) because he was insanely in love with a court dancer in Chanderi.

questions.question:
A thief is 400 m ahead of a policeman. The thief started running and policemen started chasing simultaneously. Assuming the speed of thief be 10 km/h & policemen be 15 km/h, calculate the distance (in metres) covered by the thief before the policemen caught the thief?

A. 750 m

B. 800 m

C. 850 m

D. 900 m
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6bd67c9563cdde4a0dfe99b7686282bc07365f691adfb64c907de66aebe4b011.png] 

As time is constant they cover distance according to their speed ratio

The speed of policemen - The speed of thief → Distance ahead

⇒ 15 − 10 → 400 m

⇒ 5 → 400 m

⇒ 1 → 80 m

The speed of thief = 10 km/h

⇒ 10 → 800 m

The distance (in metres) covered by the thief before the policemen caught the thief is 800m.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A thief is 400 m ahead of a policeman. The thief started running and policemen started chasing simultaneously. The speed of thief be 10 km/h & policemen be 15 km/h

**Calulation:**

Let, distance covered by thief be x km

According to the question,

x/10 = (x + 0.4)/15

⇒ x/10 – x/15 = 4/150

⇒ (3x – 2x)/30 = 2/75

⇒ x/30 = 2/75

⇒ x = 4/5

⇒ x = 0.8

∴ Distance covered by thief = 0.8 km = 0.8 × 1000 m = 800 m

questions.question:
The presence of ozone in the _____ prevents Sun's Harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiations from reaching the Earth’s surface.

A. Troposphere

B. Mesosphere

C. Stratosphere

D. Thermosphere
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Option 1**__ i.e __**C**__.

 
• **Troposphere**:

 
 
• The troposphere is the innermost layer of Earth’s atmosphere.
 
• Constantly changing and mixing up the gases takes place in this part of our atmosphere.
 
• This layer has the air we breathe and the clouds in the sky.
 
 
 
• **Stratosphere**:
 
 
• The stratosphere is located above the troposphere and below the mesosphere.
 
• There are no storms or turbulence here to mix up the air, so cold, heavy air is at the bottom and warm, light air is at the top.
 
• **The ozone layer found in this stratosphere helps protect us from ultraviolet radiation (UV) from the sun by blocking UV radiations from reaching the Earth’s surface**

questions.question: Which mirror is preferred as a rear-view (wing) mirror in vehicles because of its wider field of view?
questions.solution:
**Option 1** is the correct answer: __**Convex mirror**__ is used as a **rearview mirror** in the vehicle.

__**CONCEPT**__:

__
 
• Plane mirror: This mirror is straight without any inward or outward curve.

 
 
• It forms a virtual image and upright image which is of size as same as the object.
 
• The bathroom mirrors are an example.
 
 
 
• Concave mirror: The mirrors curved inside on the reflecting side are called concave mirrors.
 
 
• These mirrors produce a real, inverted, and magnified image of the object.
 
• Thes are used in reflecting telescopes, shaving mirrors, and ophthalmoscope.
 
 

 
• **Convex mirror**: It is an **outward curved mirror** that produces a **diminished image**.

 
 
• Convex mirrors either diverge a parallel beam of light into all directions or gather light from all directions and produce a parallel beam out of it.
 
 

**EXPLANATION**__:

 
• **Following are the reasons** as to why a **convex mirror** is used as a **rearview mirror** in the vehicle

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e419353f8ea686c4f52bc0ef3be89518be5993f1edd2fccbde193c14d74d401a.png] 

 
• The image formed by the convex mirror is **virtual and erect** in contrast to that of the real but inverted image of the concave mirror.
 
• It **gathers light from all directions** and aligns it as a parallel beam so that it provides a wider view to the viewer. That's why the **convex mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles.** So option 1 is correct.

questions.question: Which of the following is the outermost part of human skin?
questions.solution:
**Option 1** is the correct answer: __**Epidermis**__ is the **outermost part** of human skin.

 
• Skin is a sensory organ that gives the sensation of touch.
 
• It is the** largest external organ** of the human body.
 
• It acts as a shield between internal organs and the outer world.
 
• It has been divided into three layers epidermis, dermis, and hypodermis.

**Epidermis**:

 
• It is the outermost layer of our skin.
 
• It contains **melanocytes** that produce the pigment called **melanin**.
 
• The thickness of the epidermis varies from** 0.05mm to 1.5mm**.

**Dermis**:

 
• Beneath the epidermis is located another layer called Dermis.
 
• It is the **thickest **layer of our skin (1.5mm to 4mm thick).
 
• It contains structures like **hair follicles, blood vessels, lymph vessels, sweat glands, sebaceous glands, and nerve endings**.
 
• It also contains two important proteins **elastin and collagen**.
 
• Collagen is found in connective tissues between internal organs, muscles, and skin.
 
• Elastin provides elasticity to the skin and brings back it to the original position after being pulled or stretched.

**Hypodermis**:

 
• This innermost layer of the skin is also known as a **subcutis or subcutaneous** layer.
 
• It is made up of **fat cells and collagen**.
 
• It is the insulating layer of the skin and also acts as a shock absorber.

**Nerve Fibre**:

 
• It is a long** thread-like cytoplasmic projection of a nerve cell** in vertebrates.
 
• It conducts the electrochemical impulses or action potential away from the nerve cell.

questions.question:
In a right-angled triangle, the hypotenuse is 2 cm longer than the perpendicular which is 2 cm longer than the base. Calculate the length of the base.

A) 6 cm

B) 9 cm

C) 10 cm

D) 8 cm
questions.solution:
Let, length of the base = x cm

Length of perpendicular = (x + 2) cm

Length of hypotenuse = (x + 4) cm

According to the questions,

⇒ x² + (x + 2)² = (x + 4)²

⇒ x² + x² + 4x + 4 = x² + 8x + 16

⇒ x² – 4x – 12 = 0

⇒ x² – 6x + 2x – 12 = 0

⇒ x(x – 6) + 2(x – 6) = 0

⇒ (x – 6) (x + 2) = 0

⇒ x = 6 or – 2

∴ Length of the base = 6 cm
